role: The connection: a Netty channel handler that queues inbound packets for the game thread, dispatches outbound ones, tracks the protocol state, and is the place the oracle's lockstep barrier counts sends and receives.
scope_reason: Wire format and connection plumbing: native messages are structs by design (SPEC: messages are structs, not bytes) (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md).

members.name: isClientSide
members.note: No channel objects exist natively; the tick is split into a client half and a server half with explicit delivery phases.

members.name: receivedPacketsQueue
members.note: The queue's effect survives as the message structs the client half hands the server half (struct client_out, struct s2c_pkt); no queue object.

members.name: outboundPacketsQueue
members.note: Only used when the channel is not yet open; the local channel is open from the join.

members.name: channel
members.note: Netty plumbing, replaced by struct delivery.

members.name: netHandler
members.note: The handler role is the native tick's server half (player.c, survival.c).

members.name: connectionState
members.note: The native connection is always in PLAY after the join; no protocol state machine.

members.name: field_152463_r
members.note: Encryption-enabled flag; never set.

members.name: attrKeyConnectionState
members.note: Static channel attribute; Netty plumbing.

members.name: attrKeyReceivable
members.note: Static channel attribute.

members.name: attrKeySendable
members.note: Static channel attribute.

members.name: eventLoops
members.note: Static thread pool; the native tick is single-threaded by design.

members.name: field_152462_h
members.note: The shared statistics object; telemetry only.

members.name: NetworkManager
members.note: Just records the side flag.

members.name: channelActive
members.note: Channel open bookkeeping; the native join is the snapshot load.

members.name: channelRead0
members.note: Queue-or-process plus the oracle's Lockstep.onRecv hook; the native delivery phase replaces both.

members.name: scheduleOutboundPacket
members.note: The native send is a struct push onto the tick's s2c list; no channel, no listeners.

members.name: dispatchPacket
members.note: Carries the oracle's Lockstep.onSend hook; the native push is the delivery itself.

members.name: processReceivedPackets
members.note: Drain the queue into the handler; the native tick's deliver phase does the same work in a fixed order.

members.name: closeChannel
members.note: No disconnect path in the native session.

members.name: isLocalChannel
members.note: Always true in the oracle (LocalChannel); the native engine assumes it.

members.name: provideLanClient
members.note: Remote TCP connect; unused in-process.

members.name: provideLocalClient
members.note: The connect the integrated server uses; the native join replaces it.

members.name: enableEncryption
members.note: Online-mode only; never called here.

missing: The Netty transport itself (queues, channel, protocol-state attributes, dispatch): replaced by the native tick's struct-message phases; its observable role, the lockstep barrier, lives in the oracle's Lockstep hooks and the native tick's fixed client-deliver, server-tick, server-deliver order.
notes: The nested InboundHandlerTuplePacketListener is the outbound queue's entry type. This file is where the harness's determinism hooks sit (Lockstep.onRecv/onSend), so its behavior is gated by every tape even though no native counterpart exists.
